scenes.text: A 4096 by 4096 picture in a single pass. What does the transformer have to do, and can a 3080 keep up?
scenes.say: A picture four thousand pixels on a side, in one pass, with no enlarging pass. What does the transformer have to do to draw it? And can a gaming card keep up?

scenes.headline: How MiniMax H3-Image draws sixteen megapixels
scenes.sub: Rows, references, and what offloading really costs
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Elowen! MiniMax just opened the weights of its image model. Let's count what a sixteen megapixel picture costs it.

scenes.title: From noise to rows
scenes.sub: How a diffusion transformer makes an image
scenes.say: Chapter one. From noise to rows.

steps.term: Encoder: turns the prompt into vectors
steps.say: The prompt goes through a thirty two billion parameter vision language model, and the generator reads its fiftieth layer.
Text rows and noisy image rows are packed into one sequence. Fifty transformer blocks attend over all of it at once.
After six denoising steps, the image decoder turns the latent back into pixels.

parts.say: Flow matching draws a straight line from noise to a clean latent.
At t of one the latent is clean. At zero it is pure noise.
The network learns the velocity along that line, and sampling follows it in six distilled steps, each with its own output head.

steps.term: Latent: the compressed grid the model draws
steps.say: The image encoder shrinks each side sixteen times and keeps twenty four channels per spot.
Every two by two patch becomes one row, so each row covers thirty two by thirty two pixels. That is sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four rows.
Add a five hundred and twelve token prompt, and every block attends over almost seventeen thousand rows.

scenes.title: Why 16 MP is hard
scenes.sub: Attention grows with the square of the rows
scenes.say: Chapter two. Why sixteen megapixels is hard.

scenes.title: Rows grow with area, attention with its square

params.left: the canvas, one patch per row
params.right: attention: every row against every row

steps.say: Here is a canvas cut into patches, one row each. Every row has to compare itself with every other row.
Double the side, and there are four times the rows. The comparison square grows sixteen times.

steps.term: Quadratic: doubling rows quadruples the work
steps.say: At four thousand pixels a side, attention has grown from a sliver of each step to well over a third of it.

scenes.label: for one sampling step at 4096 by 4096
scenes.note: about six thousand trillion operations for the whole image
scenes.say: Counted from the config, one step at that size is about a thousand and sixty one trillion operations. Six steps make the picture.

scenes.title: Where the 33.1B parameters sit
scenes.say: And the thirty three billion parameters? Thirty nine percent only compute per-step modulation from the timestep. With six fixed steps, they collapse into small tables.

scenes.title: An edit, as the transformer sees it

steps.say: Each reference image goes in twice. Once through the vision encoder, as about a thousand tokens beside the prompt.
And once through the image encoder, as latent rows held almost clean for every step.
The target sits after them. To the transformer, an edit with three references looks like a short video whose last frame is being drawn.
Here MiniMax gives it ten references, an empty room and nine catalogue shots.
One edit puts every piece in the room. Up to sixteen references are allowed, and each one adds rows and quadratic cost.

scenes.title: The 3080 question
scenes.sub: Offloading is cheap. Compute is not.
scenes.say: Chapter four. The gaming card question.

scenes.title: One 4096 step on a 10 GB 3080
scenes.say: Stream the twelve gigabyte checkpoint over the card's link every step, and the copy takes half a second. The arithmetic takes about forty five. Offloading hides behind compute.

scenes.title: What the release leaves out
scenes.say: On paper it fits, at three to four and a half minutes an image. Nobody has timed it on that card. And the release has gaps.

items.say: There is no benchmark behind strongest instruction following. Only a curated gallery.
The licence excludes the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom and Korea.
And its commercial gate fell from twenty million dollars to one million, with any hosted service needing permission.

scenes.text: At 16 MP every block has thousands of rows to chew, so the weight copies hide. The card's arithmetic sets the time.
scenes.mark: The card's arithmetic sets the time
scenes.say: At sixteen megapixels every block has thousands of rows to chew, so the weight copies hide. The card's arithmetic sets the time.
To recap. Sixteen megapixels is about sixteen thousand rows. References are just more rows. And on a gaming card, expect minutes, not seconds.
